name: Platelet-rich fibrin for hair

lead: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is made by spinning your own blood to form a platelet- and white-cell-rich fibrin clot, a relative of PRP. People try it on the scalp hoping for thicker-looking hair.

The platelets in the clot release growth factors such as PDGF, TGF-beta and VEGF, and the fibrin acts as a scaffold near follicles. PRF is documented mainly in dental and oral surgery; for hair, one small registered trial of 10 participants compares it with PRP in female pattern hair loss, with no results published.

paras: It is an in-clinic procedure: blood is drawn, spun into a clot, and the material is placed in the scalp, much like PRP sessions. It is offered as an off-label aesthetic treatment, usually as a series of visits.
It is an injection-based procedure using your own blood. Risks specific to hair use are not described in published sources, and it is off-label for hair.

angle.text: Users and clinics try PRF on thinning scalp hair as a relative of PRP, hoping growth factors released near the follicles will thicken hair. It is documented mainly in dentistry, and one small registered trial has looked at hair.

lead: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is a preparation made from a person's own blood that concentrates platelets and white blood cells in a fibrin matrix. It is described as a derivative of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and is documented mainly as a tissue-engineering scaffold in oral and maxillofacial surgery [1]. Its use for hair restoration is a newer, off-label application discussed in aesthetic medicine.

Only a very small amount of registered human research exists on PRF for hair: a single listed trial with 10 participants compares PRF and PRP in female pattern hair loss [2]. No results are published in the sources reviewed here.

paras: According to Wikipedia, blood is drawn into tubes without anticoagulant and centrifuged immediately for a few minutes. Three layers form: platelet-poor plasma on top, a PRF clot in the middle and red blood cells at the bottom. The clot is removed and trimmed [1]. Platelet activation during preparation releases growth factors such as PDGF, TGF-beta, VEGF and epidermal growth factor, and the article argues the fibrin matrix is key to its therapeutic potential [1].

In aesthetic practice PRF is discussed as an alternative to PRP for scalp treatment in hair thinning. The documented clinical applications in the encyclopedic literature are dental, such as socket preservation, sinus lift and periodontal regeneration, and hair is not mentioned there [1].

One registered trial, started in May 2023 with 10 participants, is titled as an efficacy and safety study of PRF and PRP in female pattern hair loss; its status is listed as unknown [2]. A separate registered study of platelet-rich therapy for abdominoplasty scar revision is not about hair [3]. No published results for hair were found.
